title: HTTP/3 RFC 9114 Positive Floor Verification
verification_method: Focused requirement-home tests, HTTP/3 frame and stream tests, SETTINGS and header-validation tests, minimal client/server loopback tests, advisory local h3spec subset evidence, BenchmarkDotNet frame-writer before/after evidence, local ProtocolLab source-root selection attempt, SpecTrace JSON validation, and diff hygiene for the HTTP/3 positive floor.
scope: This verification covers the HTTP/3 positive floor: frame parsing and writing, stream classification, control-stream sequencing, SETTINGS exchange, header validation, and the minimal client/server request-response path. It does not verify interop matrix promotion or external peer behavior.
preconditions: The repo remains in the JSON-only SpecTrace workflow.
The HTTP/3 package stays independent from ASP.NET hosting concerns.
procedure: For standalone frame-writer changes, run `dotnet run -c Release --project benchmarks/Incursa.Quic.Benchmarks.csproj -- --job Short --filter "*FrameWriter_Write*" --artifacts .artifacts/perf/<run>/bdn-before --inProcess` before the implementation change and rerun with `--artifacts .artifacts/perf/<run>/bdn-after` after the implementation change.

Attempt local ProtocolLab validation through the source-root loop when the active ProtocolLab inventory still contains a QUIC.NET HTTP/3 implementation cell; otherwise record the inventory-selection blocker instead of creating ad hoc package-template state.
expected_result: The focused HTTP/3 tests pass, the requirement-home tests confirm trace linkage for the HTTP/3 positive floor, core SpecTrace JSON validation accepts the new artifacts, and no whitespace hygiene issues are introduced.
status_summary: The managed HTTP/3 positive floor is trace-owned by canonical RFC 9114 artifacts and is covered by focused frame, stream, SETTINGS, header-validation, and loopback client/server tests. Frame parsing and writing proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S4-0002` now directly classifies positive DATA, HEADERS, SETTINGS, GOAWAY, CANCEL_PUSH, MAX_PUSH_ID, and PUSH_PROMISE round trips, negative malformed frame lengths and duplicate SETTINGS cases, request-stream frame-type rejection before payload-specific parsing, and edge partial-buffer, exact-length, unknown-frame, and reserved-frame preservation. Stream lifecycle proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S6-0001` now classifies bidirectional request mapping, unidirectional stream type parsing, one-control-stream-per-endpoint enforcement, SETTINGS-first control-stream sequencing, invalid frame rejection per stream kind, gated push handling, and loopback peer control-stream observation. SETTINGS exchange proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S7-0001` classifies one-time local emission, peer settings capture, known QPACK and max-field-section settings, ignored allowed unknown settings, and rejection of duplicate or reserved HTTP/2 setting identifiers. Header validation proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S8-0001` classifies common request/response headers, malformed pseudo-header and forbidden field rejection, content-length mismatch rejection, trailer validation, and request/response message sequencing including informational responses. Request-response floor proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S9-0001` classifies static and dynamic-QPACK loopback success, ALPN rejection, protocol-invalid request parsing as peer-visible HTTP/3/QPACK application close, missing-route 404 behavior, no-request-FIN dispatch, and recovery after an abrupt stream reset. The client observes peer unidirectional control streams for SETTINGS and GOAWAY and rejects new request streams after an observed server GOAWAY cutoff. The 2026-06-19 advisory local h3spec subset evidence reduced mapped HTTP/3/QPACK failures from 15 to 6 after the protocol-close slice; a later qlog-retained subset run under `.artifacts/http3-h3spec/20260619T0410Z-slice3-cancel-push-qlog` reported the CANCEL_PUSH-on-request-stream case passing after request-stream raw frame-type validation, with three remaining mapped failures. The qlog-retained subset run under `.artifacts/http3-h3spec/20260619T0645Z-qpack-boundary-http3-qlog` reported all RFC 9114 cases in the 15-case HTTP/3-matched subset passing, with only the RFC 9204 QPACK 4.2 advisory residual remaining; the report SHA256 is `A58EF1B588E498230B0F04AC1C4E567B3B8A8B8A4F64878A38BC89ED0427626D` and the results SHA256 is `F14C06A0E9D7B12A692E16662FB4F6EFCABC5500FD22FD71D4BFDDD8CB606041`. The h3spec evidence remains local advisory conformance triage, not support promotion. External peer promotion remains a separate interop concern.

supplemental_sections.heading: Client Peer Control Stream Evidence
supplemental_sections.content: On 2026-06-10, the HTTP/3 client gained peer unidirectional stream observation for the existing RFC 9114 control-stream surface. The client classifies server control streams through `Http3StreamDispatcher`, emits peer SETTINGS diagnostics, records GOAWAY from the server control stream, and rejects later client request attempts at or above the advertised GOAWAY stream ID with `H3_REQUEST_REJECTED`. Focused verification passed `dotnet test tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests.csproj -c Release --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Http3StreamDispatcherTests|FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalClientTests|FullyQualifiedName~REQ_QUIC_RFC9114_0002"` with 37/37 tests. BenchmarkDotNet Dry validation for `*Http3AllocationPathBenchmarks.ControlStream*` completed successfully to prove the added control-stream benchmarks compile and execute; that Dry run is not performance evidence or a public benchmark claim.

supplemental_sections.heading: Local h3spec Protocol-Close Evidence
supplemental_sections.content: On 2026-06-19, `Http3Server` began mapping server-side `Http3Exception` and `QPackException` parser failures to QUIC application close codes instead of attempting a 400 response for protocol-invalid wire input. Focused local verification passed `dotnet test tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.RequestDataBeforeHeaders|FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.TruncatedRequestFrame|FullyQualifiedName~Http3LowLevelProtocolTests|FullyQualifiedName~Http3QPackErrorHandlingMatrixTests"` with 35/35 tests. The local acquired h3spec subset run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\interop\http3-h3spec\Run-H3Spec.ps1 -RunId 20260619T0212Z-slice1-http3-close -AcquireH3Spec -NoBuild -NoValidateCertificate -TimeoutMilliseconds 5000 -Match "HTTP/3"` executed 15 mapped HTTP/3/QPACK cases and reported 6 failures. The report SHA256 is `4DD585621AE019684649E65BD5658ABF5FA90C15B2F457D12085D6CFC4D14338`; the results SHA256 is `1FBA9ABB5AFDEA5FA0FBC8C3C9201A8AA12CA44C239FF9EC30ED9754710C2631`. This is local advisory conformance triage only.

supplemental_sections.heading: Local h3spec Request-Frame Evidence
supplemental_sections.content: On 2026-06-19, request-stream frame validation began rejecting known disallowed frame types before payload-specific parsing so a malformed CANCEL_PUSH frame on a request stream maps to `H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED` rather than `H3_FRAME_ERROR`. Focused local verification passed `dotnet test tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.RequestCancelPushFrame|FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.RequestDataBeforeHeaders|FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.TruncatedRequestFrame|FullyQualifiedName~Http3LowLevelProtocolTests|FullyQualifiedName~Http3QPackErrorHandlingMatrixTests|FullyQualifiedName~Http3FrameLayerTests"` with 74/74 tests. The qlog-retained local acquired h3spec subset run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\interop\http3-h3spec\Run-H3Spec.ps1 -RunId 20260619T0410Z-slice3-cancel-push-qlog -AcquireH3Spec -NoBuild -NoValidateCertificate -TimeoutMilliseconds 5000 -Match "HTTP/3"` executed 15 mapped HTTP/3/QPACK cases and reported 3 failures; the CANCEL_PUSH-on-request-stream case passed. The report SHA256 is `6C5E18BB30C89F2CCE58D50DB4DAFF8FF56EEB6251CA18A87C75BDDD6C15ACCD`; the results SHA256 is `6A5DB732924279318823B0968236D8721A1039CD74EC12F43DD73FF2FFEC8A03`. This is local advisory conformance triage only.

supplemental_sections.heading: Local h3spec HTTP/3 Residual Reduction
supplemental_sections.content: On 2026-06-19, peer-observable regression coverage for malformed request framing, duplicate pseudo-headers, control-stream invalid frames, duplicate SETTINGS, invalid QPACK static table references, and QPACK encoder capacity errors preceded the qlog-retained local h3spec subset run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\interop\http3-h3spec\Run-H3Spec.ps1 -RunId 20260619T0645Z-qpack-boundary-http3-qlog -AcquireH3Spec -NoBuild -NoValidateCertificate -TimeoutMilliseconds 5000 -Match "HTTP/3"`. That run executed 15 mapped HTTP/3/QPACK cases and reported one RFC 9204 residual; all RFC 9114 cases in the subset passed. The report SHA256 is `A58EF1B588E498230B0F04AC1C4E567B3B8A8B8A4F64878A38BC89ED0427626D`; the results SHA256 is `F14C06A0E9D7B12A692E16662FB4F6EFCABC5500FD22FD71D4BFDDD8CB606041`. This is local advisory conformance triage only.

supplemental_sections.heading: Standalone Frame Writer Evidence
supplemental_sections.content: On 2026-06-09, the standalone HTTP/3 frame writer was tightened to allocate the exact encoded frame length for `Http3FrameWriter.WriteFrame(ulong, ReadOnlySpan<byte>)`. Focused `Http3FrameLayerTests` passed 38/38, and the adjacent HTTP/3 positive-floor filter for frame layer, minimal client/server, and `REQ_QUIC_RFC9114_0002` passed 70/70. BenchmarkDotNet Short before/after evidence for the added `FrameWriter_Write*` benchmarks showed `FrameWriter_WritePlaintextResponseHeaders` moving from 290.8 ns and 392 B to 30.57 ns and 80 B, `FrameWriter_WritePlaintextResponseData` from 293.8 ns and 352 B to 14.92 ns and 40 B, and `FrameWriter_WriteLargeDataFrame16Kb` from 42639.1 ns and 81920 B to 1174.73 ns and 16416 B. These are local microbenchmark samples and should not be treated as published end-to-end throughput claims.

supplemental_sections.heading: ProtocolLab Local Loop Note
supplemental_sections.content: The repo-local source-root ProtocolLab loop was attempted on 2026-06-09 with `scripts/perf/Invoke-ProtocolLabLocalQuicBenchmark.ps1 -UseProjectReferences -Suite h3-local-v1-comparison -WorkflowProfile Quick -Scenarios http3.core.status,http3.payload.bytes.64kb -NoRestore`, but the current ProtocolLab script surface rejected the wrapper-emitted `-IncursaQuicSourceRoot` parameter before running benchmarks. A direct ProtocolLab CLI run with `-p:IncursaQuicSourceRoot=C:\shared\src\incursa\quic-dotnet` and `--implementations incursa-http3` then reported `No run cells were selected`; both checked local ProtocolLab inventories contain only kestrel/caddy/nginx/quic-go HTTP/3 implementation manifests after the quic-dotnet package-handoff removal. No package-template files or package uploads were used for this bounded slice.
